title: Wales today
mapAria: Map of the 22 council areas of Wales, coloured by {lens}. Use the list of council areas after the map to move between them with the keyboard.
key.label: What the colours mean
key.higherBetter: Higher is better on this measure.
key.lowerBetter: Lower is better on this measure.
key.noDirection: Neither higher nor lower is better. It is here for context.
kbd.label: Council areas, in map order
kbd.help: Arrow keys move to the nearest council area in that direction. Enter opens its figures.
panel.caption: Main figures for {name}
panel.visitHead: You can visit this place in the game
panel.visit.rhondda: In the game you can visit the Rhondda. You choose which coal tips to make safe first. It uses real records of tips, homes, schools and flood zones.
panel.visit.bethesda: In the game you can visit Bethesda and Dyffryn Ogwen. You decide who the old slate quarry is for now: homes, work, Welsh, visitors or the river.
panel.official: Official figures, from the latest open release.
explorer.title: Compare the council areas
explorer.sortHint: Press a column heading to sort by it.
explorer.caption: The 22 council areas by the measures you chose
scatter.aria: Dot chart of the 22 council areas: {x} along the bottom, {y} up the side
scatter.note: Each square is a council area. The open square is Wales. Dots that sit together do not prove one thing causes the other.
foot.honest: Real figures from the latest open data. A thinking tool, not a forecast. Not an official view.
foot.attribution: Boundaries: ONS (OGL). Terrain: AWS Terrain Tiles. Railways: OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL). Figures: ONS, Welsh Government, DESNZ (OGL).
short.coal_tips_cd: Coal tips, highest risk (C and D)
unit.pop_change: Per cent change over ten years
unit.welsh_speakers: Per cent of residents aged 3 and over
unit.deprivation: Per cent of small neighbourhoods in the poorest fifth, by the Welsh deprivation index (WIMD)
unit.deprivation_10: Per cent of small neighbourhoods in the poorest tenth, by the Welsh deprivation index (WIMD)
unit.gva_head: Value of goods and services made, per person, in pounds (GVA per head)
unit.employment: Per cent of people aged 16 to 64
unit.earnings: Pounds a week, full-time, where people live
unit.affordability: A typical house price divided by a typical year’s pay
unit.emissions_head: Tonnes of greenhouse gas a person (t CO2e)
unit.renewables: Kilowatts of clean power built, per person
unit.flood_exposure: Homes at risk for every 100 homes. A home at risk from two kinds of flood counts twice.
unit.greenspace_access: Per cent of homes within 300 m
unit.gp_travel_public: Minutes for a return trip to a GP by bus or train
unit.coal_tips_cd: Tips in the two highest risk groups, C and D
